_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor.
name: Mosquitto
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Eclipse Mosquitto is a lightweight MQTT broker for IoT devices and home automation. Clients must sign in: the user from the server's settings, plus any in the password file.
startup: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/container/mosquitto/lib PATH="/home/container/mosquitto/bin:$PATH"; if [ -n "{{MQTT_USERNAME}}" ] && [ -n "${MQTT_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then mosquitto_passwd -b passwords "{{MQTT_USERNAME}}" "$MQTT_PASSWORD" || exit 1; fi; grep -q : passwords 2>/dev/null || echo "No users yet: set Username and Password in the server's settings, or add users with mosquitto_passwd."; exec mosquitto -c mosquitto.conf

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Mosquitto: Eclipse Mosquitto publishes no Linux binaries of its own (it
# points to the distributions' packages), so this installs Debian 13's
# Mosquitto with its security updates, the same Debian the server runs:
# apt downloads the packages and checks them against Debian's signed
# archive, and they're unpacked into mosquitto/. The settings
# (mosquitto.conf), the password file and the saved messages (data/) are
# never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

# Debian 13 (trixie), signed with the archive keys the installer has.
apt="$work/apt"
mkdir -p "$apt/lists/partial" "$apt/cache/archives/partial" "$apt/parts" "$work/debs" "$work/root"
key=/usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-keyring.gpg
cat > "$apt/sources.list" <<LIST
deb [signed-by=$key] https://deb.debian.org/debian trixie main
deb [signed-by=$key] https://deb.debian.org/debian trixie-updates main
deb [signed-by=$key] https://deb.debian.org/debian-security trixie-security main
LIST
opts=(-o Dir::Etc::SourceList="$apt/sources.list" -o Dir::Etc::SourceParts="$apt/parts"
    -o Dir::State::Lists="$apt/lists" -o Dir::Cache="$apt/cache" -o Debug::NoLocking=1 -o APT::Sandbox::User=root)
echo "Reading Debian 13's package lists"
apt-get -qq "${opts[@]}" update || fail "Debian's package archive can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
# Mosquitto and the libraries it needs that the server's image lacks.
pkgs=(mosquitto libmosquitto1 libcjson1 libdlt2 libwebsockets19t64 libwrap0)
version=$(apt-cache "${opts[@]}" policy mosquitto | awk '/Candidate:/ {print $2}')
[ -n "$version" ] && [ "$version" != "(none)" ] || fail "Debian has no Mosquitto package for this CPU ($(uname -m))."

if [ -x mosquitto/bin/mosquitto ] && [ "$(cat .mosquitto-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$version" ]; then
    echo "Mosquitto $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Mosquitto $version"
    (cd "$work/debs" && apt-get -qq "${opts[@]}" download "${pkgs[@]}") || fail "The download failed. Reinstall to try again."
    for deb in "$work"/debs/*.deb; do dpkg-deb -x "$deb" "$work/root"; done
    triplet=$(ls "$work/root/usr/lib" | grep -- '-linux-gnu$' | head -n 1)
    mkdir -p "$work/new/bin" "$work/new/lib"
    cp -a "$work/root/usr/sbin/mosquitto" "$work"/root/usr/bin/mosquitto_* "$work/new/bin/"
    cp -a "$work/root/usr/lib/$triplet/." "$work/new/lib/"
    "$work/new/bin/mosquitto" -h >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ $? -eq 3 ] || true
    rm -rf mosquitto.old
    [ ! -d mosquitto ] || mv mosquitto mosquitto.old
    mv "$work/new" mosquitto
    rm -rf mosquitto.old
    echo "$version" > .mosquitto-version
fi

mkdir -p data
# A first configuration: one MQTT listener on the server's port, no
# anonymous access, and users from the password file. The port is kept up
# to date by the server's settings.
if [ ! -f mosquitto.conf ]; then
    cat > mosquitto.conf <<'CONF'
# Mosquitto's settings: https://mosquitto.org/man/mosquitto-conf-5.html
# The listener's port comes from the server's settings.
listener 1883
allow_anonymous false
password_file /home/container/passwords

persistence true
persistence_location /home/container/data/
autosave_interval 300

log_dest stdout
log_timestamp_format %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S
CONF
    echo "Wrote a first mosquitto.conf."
fi
[ -f passwords ] || { : > passwords; chmod 600 passwords; }
echo "Installed Mosquitto $version."

variables.name: Username
variables.description: A user clients can sign in as, added to the password file (or updated) at every start.
